pillars.name: Govern
pillars.description: Run the AI management system: policies, accountability, inventory, risk and impact, data and suppliers, and the metrics that show systems are under control.

pillars.name: Evaluate
pillars.description: Test systems before and after release: quality, fairness and bias (FairMind's core engines), agent behaviour and production drift.

pillars.name: Secure
pillars.description: Protect LLM applications and agents against the OWASP, MITRE ATLAS and NIST adversarial threat classes, secure the AI supply chain, defend against offensive AI and deepfakes, and respond to incidents.

pillars.name: Comply
pillars.description: Meet specific legal and certification obligations (EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001, AIUC-1 and others) and show it, through journeys that add packs up to each framework.

commonControls.name: AIMS scope, context and objectives
commonControls.objective: The organisation defines what its AI management system covers, who it serves and what it aims to achieve.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: AI policies
commonControls.objective: Current, approved policies govern how AI is built, bought and used.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: Accountability and oversight bodies
commonControls.objective: Every AI system and agent has named accountable people, and oversight bodies decide and report.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: Competence and AI literacy
commonControls.objective: People who build, operate or oversee AI are trained for their role.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: Documented information
commonControls.objective: Required records and technical documentation are controlled, current and retrievable.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: Management review and internal audit
commonControls.objective: The system is audited independently and reviewed by management at planned intervals.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: Nonconformity and corrective action
commonControls.objective: Problems are recorded, root-caused, fixed and verified as fixed.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: Regulatory applicability and change
commonControls.objective: The organisation knows which AI rules apply to each system and tracks changes to them.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: AI inventory and intake
commonControls.objective: Every AI system, agent, model and use case is registered and classified before use.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: Risk criteria, assessment and treatment
commonControls.objective: AI risks are assessed against approved criteria, treated, and residual risk is accepted by the right person.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: Impact assessment
commonControls.objective: Effects on individuals, groups, workers and society are assessed and mitigated.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: Prohibited, manipulative and misuse risks
commonControls.objective: Uses that are prohibited, manipulative or open to misuse are screened out or controlled.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Content policy compliance on harmful-content sets; manipulative design patterns; misuse scenarios in red-team runs.

commonControls.name: Data governance and provenance
commonControls.objective: Training, retrieval, synthetic and memory data have known provenance, quality and approval.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Data drift; data poisoning scan; representativeness, completeness and accuracy checks; duplicate records; personal data in training sets; poisoning scan of RAG knowledge bases.

commonControls.name: Privacy and data residency
commonControls.objective: Personal data risks and processing locations are assessed and approved.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Personal data leakage from outputs; personal data in training and retrieval sets; data residency check of processing locations.

commonControls.name: Responsible design and secure development
commonControls.objective: Systems and agents are designed and built with responsible-AI and security requirements.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: System prompt carries the required safety instructions; system prompt holds no secrets; security scan of AI-generated code.

commonControls.name: Evaluation and testing
commonControls.objective: Systems and agents are evaluated before release and when they change, with governed benchmarks.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Task accuracy on a held-out set; answer consistency; groundedness and hallucination rate; robustness to input perturbation; agent task success on scenario suites; tool-call correctness.

commonControls.name: Bias and fairness
commonControls.objective: Outcomes are tested for unfair bias across affected groups.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Group fairness metrics (selection rate, error-rate parity) per protected group; intersectional slices; counterfactual fairness; representativeness by group.

commonControls.name: Release, change and retirement
commonControls.objective: Releases, material changes and decommissioning are approved and recorded.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Release regression suite: re-runs the FMC-TST-01, FMC-FAI-01 and FMC-AGT-02 evaluations and blocks release on failure.

commonControls.name: Agent identity, access and permission bounding
commonControls.objective: Agents and people hold only the access their approved scope needs.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Least-privilege test of agent tools and extensions; attempted actions outside the approved scope are blocked; MCP server permission audit; browser-agent domain allowlist test.

commonControls.name: Threat modelling, guardrails and vulnerabilities
commonControls.objective: Threats to AI systems are modelled, guarded against at runtime and fixed when found.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Direct and indirect prompt injection; jailbreak resistance; system prompt leakage; sensitive data leakage; disclosure of tool and MCP server details; excessive agency.

commonControls.name: Human oversight and intervention
commonControls.objective: People can oversee, override, stop and be appealed to.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Kill-switch drill time to stop; human override is honoured; escalation triggers fire at the configured thresholds.

commonControls.name: Monitoring and logging
commonControls.objective: Behaviour, performance, cost and logs are monitored in operation.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Production drift and performance degradation; anomalies in tool-call patterns; cost and token thresholds; log completeness.

commonControls.name: Incidents, concerns and reporting
commonControls.objective: Incidents and concerns are handled, and reportable ones are reported on time.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Regression test for each closed incident so the failure cannot recur unseen.

commonControls.name: Transparency and disclosure
commonControls.objective: Users, affected people and the public get the information they are owed.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: AI disclosure shown where required; content provenance labels and watermarks detectable on generated output.

commonControls.name: Third parties and suppliers
commonControls.objective: AI suppliers and vendors are assessed and their terms approved.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Process evidence only: no automated evaluation; evidence is the workflow's approved record.

commonControls.name: IP, copyright and liability
commonControls.objective: Intellectual property, copyright and liability exposure from AI is reviewed.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Verbatim reproduction of copyrighted or licensed text in outputs.

commonControls.name: Environmental impact
commonControls.objective: Energy, emissions and resource use of AI are measured and reported.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Energy and emissions per inference and per training run.

commonControls.name: FairMind agent self-assurance
commonControls.objective: FairMind's own agent is governed like any other AI system in scope.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: FairMind's own agent: prompt injection, attempted unauthorised actions, completeness of the evidence trace (model and prompt versions, tool calls).

commonControls.name: Offensive AI and deepfake defence
commonControls.objective: AI-generated impersonation, fraud and manipulation aimed at the organisation is prevented, detected and verified against.
commonControls.evaluationsNeeded: Deepfake detection on inbound media; voice-clone resistance of voice authentication; AI-generated phishing simulation.

steps.title: Start the run
steps.detail: Starts at the annual cycle or when a mapped regulatory or organisational change event fires.
steps.output: Run record: run ID, scope, initiator, workflow and framework versions

steps.title: Collect org context
steps.detail: Reads org profile, entities, business lines, AI system inventory summary, applicable-law register and last scope statement.
steps.failure: Connector unavailable: pause, request manual upload, label source 'manual'

steps.title: Check context and scope
steps.detail: Checks that internal and external issues, interested parties and their requirements are recorded, that the scope names in-scope entities, AI systems and roles (provider, deployer, both), and that climate relevance is considered where the climate-action amendment applies (confirm applicability).
steps.failure: Missing or ambiguous input: mark 'cannot conclude', list what is needed
steps.output: Findings, each citing a collected item

steps.title: Suggest scope statement
steps.detail: Drafts the context register, interested-party register and scope statement with each change marked.
steps.failure: Low confidence: say so on the approval card
steps.output: Proposal with rationale and confidence band

steps.title: Ask the Head of AI governance
steps.detail: Sends Head of AI governance a decision card for AIMS context and scope: what would change, why, the risk if approved, the agent's confidence band and links to the evidence. Gate: Approve / approve with edits / request changes (max 3 rounds) / reject. SoD: Approver is not the run initiator

next.label: changes asked: max 3 rounds then escalate

steps.failure: Approver unreachable: deny by default, nothing recorded or changed
steps.output: Decision record: approver, time, outcome, comments, justification

steps.title: Record scope
steps.detail: Saves the approved context register and scope statement as a new controlled version.
steps.failure: Write fails: stop, no partial changes, escalate

steps.title: Revise
steps.detail: Reworks the proposal using the approver's comments. Maximum 3 rounds, then escalates.
steps.failure: Round 4: escalate

steps.title: Escalate
steps.detail: Notifies the approver's delegate or manager; run stays paused; nothing is recorded or changed.
steps.failure: No delegate: notify Head of AI governance

steps.title: File evidence
steps.detail: Files context register, interested-party register, scope statement, approval. Also files the agent trace (model and prompt versions, tool calls), hashed, against: ISO/IEC 42001 4.1; ISO/IEC 42001 4.2; ISO/IEC 42001 4.3; ISO/IEC 42001 4.4; NIST AI RMF 1.0 GOVERN 1.1; CSA AI Controls Matrix GRC; ...

patterns.name: AI management system scope and objectives
patterns.objective: What the AI management system covers and what it must achieve.

patterns.name: AI policies
patterns.objective: AI, acceptable-use and customer data policies kept current and approved.

patterns.name: Accountability and oversight bodies
patterns.objective: Named owners, an ethics committee and board reporting.

patterns.name: Competence and AI literacy
patterns.objective: Role-based training for people who build, run or oversee AI.

patterns.name: AI inventory and intake
patterns.objective: Every system and use case registered and classified before use.

patterns.name: Lifecycle and change control
patterns.objective: Responsible design, release gates, material change and retirement.

patterns.name: Risk management
patterns.objective: Risk appetite and criteria, taxonomy, assessment, treatment and residual acceptance.

patterns.name: Impact assessment
patterns.objective: Effects on individuals, groups and society assessed and mitigated.

patterns.name: Data governance
patterns.objective: Provenance, quality, retrieval, synthetic and fine-tuning data, retention and disposal.

patterns.name: Privacy and residency
patterns.objective: Privacy risk and processing locations approved.

patterns.name: Third parties, IP and liability
patterns.objective: Vendors, copyright and licensing, insurance and liability.

patterns.name: Governance metrics, cost and sustainability
patterns.objective: Cost, consumption and environmental impact tracked.

patterns.name: Quality and reliability
patterns.objective: Accuracy, consistency, groundedness, robustness, calibration, uncertainty and reproducibility.

patterns.name: Independent testing and benchmarks
patterns.objective: Third-party testing and governed benchmarks.

patterns.name: Fairness and bias
patterns.objective: FairMind's core: group, intersectional, counterfactual, LLM, India-specific and multilingual bias, and fairness drift.

patterns.name: Data quality evaluation
patterns.objective: Drift, poisoning, representativeness, completeness, duplicates, personal data, labels and lineage.

patterns.name: Explainability and oversight testing
patterns.objective: Explanations, overrides, escalation and human-in-the-loop design tested.

patterns.name: Agent evaluation
patterns.objective: Agent task success, tool-call correctness and stopping on command.

patterns.name: Production monitoring
patterns.objective: Drift, degradation, anomalies, runaway detection and log completeness in operation.

patterns.name: Use-case evaluation suites
patterns.objective: Ready-made suites for hiring, credit, finance, health, customer service, coding agents, public benefits, education and insurance.

patterns.name: Prompt and input security
patterns.objective: Prompt injection, jailbreaks, system prompt protection and prompt governance (OWASP LLM01, LLM07).

patterns.name: Output handling and data leakage
patterns.objective: Unsafe output sinks, leakage, embeddings and redaction (OWASP LLM02, LLM05, LLM08).

patterns.name: Secure AI development and vulnerabilities
patterns.objective: Secure development, vulnerability handling and coding agents.

patterns.name: Agent identity and least privilege
patterns.objective: Agent suitability, identity, permissions, access reviews and delegation (OWASP ASI03).

patterns.name: MCP, tools and browser agents
patterns.objective: MCP servers, tool poisoning, secrets, shadow servers and browser agents (OWASP MCP Top 10, ASI02).

patterns.name: Multi-agent and memory security
patterns.objective: Agent topology, inter-agent trust and memory poisoning (OWASP ASI06, ASI07).

patterns.name: Agent containment and rogue agents
patterns.objective: Threat models, runaway limits, cascading failures, rogue agents and trust exploitation (OWASP ASI08, ASI09, ASI10).

patterns.name: AI supply chain
patterns.objective: AI-BOM, model intake, model file scanning and backdoor detection (OWASP LLM03, ASI04).

patterns.name: Adversarial ML and red teaming
patterns.objective: Red teaming, extraction, inversion, evasion and reconnaissance (MITRE ATLAS, NIST AI 100-2).

patterns.name: Offensive AI and deepfake defence
patterns.objective: Impersonation, deepfakes, voice clones, AI phishing, provenance labels and manipulation.

patterns.name: Content safety
patterns.objective: Harmful, abusive, CBRN and manipulative content, and misuse.

patterns.name: AI incident response
patterns.objective: Concerns, incidents, containment, communication and regression tests.

patterns.name: FairMind agent self-assurance
patterns.objective: FairMind's own agent governed and tested like any other.

patterns.name: Applicability and prohibited practices
patterns.objective: Which rules apply to each system, tracking changes, and screening out prohibited uses.

patterns.name: Conformity, documentation and registration
patterns.objective: Technical documentation, conformity and registration, and GPAI duties.

patterns.name: Transparency and regulatory reporting
patterns.objective: Disclosure to users, public transparency reports and serious-incident reporting.

patterns.name: Audit and certification readiness
patterns.objective: Controlled documents, internal audit, management review and corrective action.

patterns.name: Rights of affected people
patterns.objective: Explanation and appeal, worker consultation and accessibility.
